cards.alt: Sample multiple choice card: Which paragraph note is best for a passage map?

questions.stem: A stem reads: "Which of the following findings, if true, would most weaken the author's claim that tutoring raises exam scores?" What kind of question is this?
options: A main idea question in Foundations of Comprehension
A new information (weaken) question in Reasoning Beyond the Text
A function question in Reasoning Within the Text
A tone question in Foundations of Comprehension
questions.explanation: B is correct. The stem brings in a hypothetical finding to test the argument, which is the signature of new information questions. A (Misclassified question type): Main idea stems ask what the passage is about as a whole, with no hypothetical finding. C (Misclassified question type): Function stems ask why the author mentions something already in the passage. D (Misclassified question type): Tone stems ask about the author's attitude, not about outside evidence.

questions.stem: After 30 minutes you have finished only two of nine passages. The best adjustment is:
options: Speed up slightly and guess and flag hard questions sooner
Stop mapping entirely so that you can read faster
Restart passage three from the top to settle in
Skip passages seven through nine to catch up
questions.explanation: A is correct. A small pace increase plus earlier triage recovers time without sacrificing the remaining passages. B (Overcorrection): Dropping mapping entirely may cost accuracy; a small adjustment is enough. C (True but irrelevant): Rereading spends time on work already done. D (Overcorrection): Giving up three passages is a larger sacrifice than the situation needs.

questions.stem: In the sentence "Since wages rose, spending must have risen," the clause "wages rose" is:
options: The main conclusion of the sentence
A concession granted to an opponent
Evidence offered for the conclusion
A counterargument to the main claim
questions.explanation: C is correct. Since marks the following clause as support for the claim that spending rose. A (Reversal): The conclusion is that spending rose, which follows the comma. B (Distortion): Nothing is granted to an opponent. D (Distortion): No opposing view is presented.

questions.stem: Evidence: every employee who attended the seminar later received a promotion. Conclusion: the seminar helps careers. Which is a required assumption?
options: Seminars are always useful.
Promotions are the best measure of career success.
Employees enjoyed the seminar.
The promotions were not caused by something other than the seminar.
questions.explanation: D is correct. If another factor produced the promotions, the seminar's effect is not shown. Denying this assumption breaks the argument. A (Extreme language): The argument does not need such a broad claim. B (Extreme language): The argument needs only that promotions count as career success, not that they are the best measure. C (True but irrelevant): Enjoyment is not the link between attendance and promotion.

questions.stem: Two choices remain on a detail question. One uses the passage's exact words but reverses cause and effect. The other paraphrases correctly. You should choose:
options: The paraphrase, because the reversal is a trap
The exact-word choice, because it matches the text
Neither, and skip the question
Whichever is longer
questions.explanation: A is correct. Matching meaning matters more than matching words. B (Surface match): Repeated wording is a lure; its meaning is reversed. C (Overcorrection): One of the two is supported, so you can answer. D (True but irrelevant): Length is not evidence.

demo_cards.back: A short margin note per paragraph (3 to 6 words) that records what the paragraph does, not what it says in detail.

demo_cards.text: A passage map has four parts: the {{c1::topic}}, a {{c2::purpose note per paragraph}}, the author's {{c3::tone}}, and the {{c4::main idea}}.
demo_cards.extra: These are the four things a finished map records.

demo_cards.stem: An author writes that a policy is "well meant but poorly built." The tone is best described as:
options: Scathing condemnation
Qualified disapproval
Laudatory endorsement
Detached indifference
demo_cards.why: The phrase gives credit (well meant) and criticism (poorly built). Scathing overshoots; laudatory ignores the criticism; indifferent ignores the opinion words.

demo_cards.statement: A passage map should record every statistic so you can answer detail questions.
demo_cards.why: The map records purpose. Details are looked up in the text when a question asks, which is faster than recording them.
